reconstructed_theorem_text:
Let E be the full finite-dimensional real Hilbert space with its Borel measurable structure and canonical full-space Lebesgue/Haar volume, including dimension zero. The approved ambient instances belong to the contract; E is a connected real vector space and the full-space volume is nonzero.
Let u:E->R be locally integrable with respect to this volume. Assume that for every real C1 compactly supported test psi:E->R and every direction a:E, the actual function x->u(x)*(fderiv R psi x a) is volume-integrable and
  integral u(x)*(fderiv R psi x a) dx = 0.
Then there exists ONE real c such that u(x)=c for volume-almost every x in E.
Local integrability is ordinary volume-local L1, not a global-volume L1 requirement. The derivative is the genuine real Frechet derivative of the C1 test function, not a totalized zero derivative asserted for the rough u. The same c works on the whole space, not a separately chosen value on each neighborhood/test/direction; c may depend on u. The conclusion is an almost-everywhere equality, not pointwise constancy or classical differentiability of u. No mollifier, sequence, or derivative certificate is an input. No disconnected-domain analogue, uniqueness assertion, weighted operator-domain converse, spectral gap or additional functional inequality is an explicit conclusion.
objects: Full real Hilbert/Borel E and nonzero canonical volume; actual locally volume-integrable real function u; all real C1 compact-support tests psi and directions a; one existential real constant c.
domains: Full finite-dimensional connected real vector space E,including dimension zero; u:E->R. LocallyIntegrable and all Integrable/integrals are actual ordinary full-space volume. Test Frechet derivatives are real and genuine. AE equality is volume-AE on the whole E,not on a disconnected subset or under another law.
quantifiers: Universally over approved ambient E and real u satisfying local integrability and forall psi:E->R,C1 psi -> compact support -> forall a:E,Integrable(u*Dpsi[a]) and zero integral. Then exists ONE real c before the whole-space volume-AE equality. c may depend on u,not on each test/direction/neighborhood.
assumptions: Actual ordinary volume LocallyIntegrable u; every C1 compact real psi/every a has the legal L1 product u(x)*fderiv R psi x a and its volume integral exactly zero. Full finite-dimensional connected E with canonical nonzero volume,including0. No global L1,classical derivative of rough u,pointwise fderiv-zero or mollifier/sequence premise.
conclusion: Exists c:R with u volume-almost everywhere equal to the actual constant function x->c on all E.
scopes: Whole-space weak directional derivative-zero gives one volume-AE constant. Neither pointwise equality nor uniqueness of c is an explicit conclusion. No disconnected-domain replacement; no weighted-domain/kernel converse,spectral gap,centered/range/functional inequality or core/main/composition claim.
constant_dependencies: No quantitative constant,curvature parameter or positive dimension requirement. Existential c is any real and may depend on u. Derivative-integral RHS is exactly zero,with unit product coefficient; all directions universally quantified.
